1.why: The UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with clear letter spacing and comfortable line spacing across all screens.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case with no italics, all-caps, or dense text blocks.

3.why: The card-based layout is simple, uncluttered, and readable at mobile width.

4.why: Copy is brief and plain, e.g. “Sign in to begin. Take your time.” and “Enter the same contact details again.”

5.why: Demo examples are shown under the email, phone, and password fields on the sign-in step.

6.why: No screen requires reading a long passage; all instructional text is one short line.

7.why: No long codes or secrets appear in the provided screens, and no copy-to-clipboard control is shown.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is offered on any screen.

9.why: Standard email and password inputs are used, which normally allow browser autofill and password managers.

10.why: Step label (e.g. Step 1 of 6) and a single prominent blue primary button make the current step and action clear.

11.why: Each screen presents only one primary action button.

12.why: After sign-in a green banner states what happened and what is next, but the later error state does not.

13.why: On-screen notes say the user can retry any step and correct details; code reveal/re-request is not shown.

14.why: The error shown is the technical message “Invalid array length,” which neither explains the problem nor how to fix it.

15.why: The UI explicitly states “No reading timer” and “Take your time,” with no countdown visible.
